mainText: This is Dose of Good for Saturday, November 14. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Molecule may help prevent diabetes-related vision loss. Researchers at Unifesp and Unesp showed the peptide Ac2-26 stopped neurons dying in human retinal cells and organoids exposed to high glucose and inflammation. Retinopathy affects more than 22% of people with diabetes. Second: Scientists find thriving wildlife in a Pacific marine sanctuary. Protected since 2025, Bikar and Bokak atolls form a 48,000 km² sanctuary. The survey found 15 seabird species, more than 260 reef fish species and nesting green turtles. Two fish may be new to science. Third: Writers launch a magazine to bring Townsville's queer community together. P. Eldridge and Michael Smith are launching CROOKED, an independent publication made by the Australian city's queer community. Writing workshops have already drawn in newcomers like Lij Bolden. Fourth: Fruit bats become allies in restoring Brazil's Atlantic Forest. These bats spread seeds of more than 140 forest plants. Researchers used synthetic fruit scents to lure them to degraded land, and 73.3% of the seeds dropped there came from pioneer species. Fifth: Scientists decode the DNA of two neglected malaria parasites. Researchers built reference genomes for P. ovale and P. malariae from patients' blood in Mali. It helps develop tests and treatments for a disease with 282 million cases in 2024. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
